metadata.scope: Public rustia project readiness, based on the current workspace and canonical design docs.
notes: Percentages are rough engineering estimates, not automated metrics.
The scope tracks public rustia crates, conformance, benchmarks, docs, tooling, and release readiness.
Project pillars and non-goals are canonical in design/02-pillars.md.
The public host-bridge remains generic; grabby-specific types and effect catalogs stay outside public rustia.

benchmark_adapters.note: mlua-lua54 runs separately from mlua-luau because both mlua-sys builds use links = "lua"; mlua-luau-jit is an explicit execution mode in the mlua-luau adapter family.

wasm_target_bench.note: The recurring wasm target runner executes rustia, koto, and rhai on Node/V8; the earlier four-runtime matrix is retained as historical portability evidence.

wasm_dispatch_bench.note: The recurring dispatch check runs on Node/V8; historical cross-engine evidence also found call_ref slower than br_table.

overall_goals.name: Whole public rustia project
overall_goals.state: The architecture is locked and production crates are substantial: the safe-Rust VM/compiler, pending-free pinned conformance corpus, first embedding facade with host-pluggable output/time services, CLI, benchmark matrix, private HotIR, closure-call PIC, and exact dedicated-Linux evidence are in-tree. The audit now explicitly separates that broad language coverage from the still-missing bounded object lifecycle, decision reset, the remaining host memory-telemetry/context/module/value bridge, and release packaging.
overall_goals.future_plan: Implement reclamation, quotas, OOM and reset semantics first; finish the host/module/value boundary and semantic-tail hardening; then continue measured optimization and public release work.

overall_goals.name: Usable embedded scripting crate
overall_goals.state: A useful first facade exists: typed run/compile, owned scalar/table conversions, typed host functions, retained functions/exports with generation checks, owned-value serde, extensions, hot reload, examples, diagnostics, migration guidance, and environment presets with host-pluggable stdout/clock services. It is not yet a complete rich embedding boundary: ordinary VM objects and loaded programs are retained until VM drop, there is no public decision reset, module resolver/cache, honest VM memory telemetry, graph-preserving rich values, or live zero-copy serde path.
overall_goals.future_plan: Land epoch-safe reset and bounded memory semantics, then complete internal memory telemetry, module loading, rich/live values, diagnostics, and API stabilization.

overall_goals.name: Full public standalone Luau engine release
overall_goals.state: The Luau 0.709 standalone target and 493-ref conformance denominator are strong. Release still requires bounded object/program lifetimes, aggregate memory limits and OOM behavior, deterministic lifecycle/reset semantics, a per-call host-context seam and honest memory telemetry, module loading, richer value interop, transactional installation, semantic-tail/diagnostic hardening, the full correctness/golden target matrix, and packaging. Analyzer/typechecker, raw C API, Roblox, Lua 5.4, and bytecode compatibility are not runtime-release requirements.
overall_goals.future_plan: Close the runtime lifecycle and host-boundary gates, harden the semantic tail and cross-target goldens, then package and publish against the pinned target.

overall_goals.name: Standalone benchmark OSS project
overall_goals.state: Harness, package metadata, split notes, machine-readable inventory, current-results JSON, generated claim gate, history, a standalone target-first current-results HTML report with interpreter-only and best-mode rankings plus cold-start costs, five default workload families, 18 workload entries with cross-adapter #15 string-building source coverage and six synthetic/realistic memory probes, all 12 requested adapters plus a verified mlua/Luau JIT mode, exact ephemeral-Linux fixed-throughput and evidence-only memory protocols, a recurring wasm target runner for rustia+koto+rhai on Node/V8, retained cross-engine wasm evidence, a call_ref versus br_table dispatch microbench, and an explicit dedicated-Linode native-plus-wasm matrix lifecycle are present.
overall_goals.future_plan: Split from the workspace, add the interop/serde/fuel-limit tranche and regression alerts, and accumulate longer-run public history.

overall_goals.name: Public release readiness
overall_goals.state: License, generated crate metadata audit, explicit internal dependency versions, release-preflight-enforced example compilation, first migration guide, CLI ergonomics including a line-oriented REPL, source-aware CLI diagnostics, public source-span/runtime-location error accessors, source-named facade diagnostics, typed/nested owned-table helpers, fallible host callback diagnostics, retained-handle freshness checks and current-generation accessors, host signature/fuel ABI metadata, host service presets with determinism-labeled provider sockets, release-readiness checklist, semver policy, changelog validation, release preflight, hosted CI, workflow policy checks, generated benchmark claim gating, package file-list audit, generated leaf package dry-run checks, and publishability blocker audit are present; crates are still workspace-private and release polish is incomplete.
overall_goals.future_plan: Close the bounded-memory, reset, host-service, module, value-interop, and semantic-tail runtime gates before removing publish blockers in topological order.

entries.name: Constraint and target model
entries.state: Core priorities, target matrix, and public/private boundary are documented.
entries.future_plan: Keep docs synced as implementation exposes new constraints.

entries.name: Architecture decisions
entries.state: All eight architecture axes are decided in design/30-architecture.md, the wasm pre-lock dispatch gate is closed across V8, JavaScriptCore-family, and SpiderMonkey, and the table/atom/string-slot-cache implementation plus exact dedicated-Linux validation are recorded.
entries.future_plan: Keep architecture docs synced as broader performance and realistic mixed-heap evidence lands.

entries.name: Review cleanup
entries.state: Third-party review findings are folded into canonical docs.
entries.future_plan: Treat new findings as incremental deltas, not a redesign.

entries.name: Current-state tracking
entries.state: design/CURRENT.md and this progress source now distinguish the broad conformance/performance implementation from the missing production lifecycle and host-boundary work. The latest accepted Linux cohort is the a562919 closure-call slice, following the dense/OOP/string/HotIR evidence gates.
entries.future_plan: Keep README, progress data, and design docs aligned after each major implementation slice.

entries.name: Research spikes
entries.state: Dispatch, value layout, libm determinism, GC, snapshot, and wasm-JIT directions are backed by spikes.
entries.future_plan: Keep spike outputs as evidence, but move production claims to benchmark gates.

entries.name: Luau 0.709 pin
entries.state: Target version, standalone surface, vector width, flags posture, and f64-only behavior are documented.
entries.future_plan: Watch upstream FFlag::LuauIntegerType2 and update only with explicit evidence.

entries.name: Manifest and refs
entries.state: 694 fixtures and 493 refs are executable with 0 pending rows.
entries.future_plan: Add focused fixtures for newly found gaps instead of reopening bulk inventory.

entries.name: Upstream corpus execution
entries.state: Whole upstream Luau 0.709 conformance scripts are represented through executable fixtures.
entries.future_plan: Preserve green status while hardening engine internals.

entries.name: Harness and coverage notes
entries.state: Runner, manifest validation, and detailed coverage notes are in-tree.
entries.future_plan: Add coverage metadata for new public-parity features as they land.

entries.name: Lexer
entries.state: Production lexer crate exists with tests.
entries.future_plan: Expand edge-case coverage as conformance finds parser/lexer gaps.

entries.name: Parser
entries.state: Hand-written parser handles Luau syntax and type-grammar erasure.
entries.future_plan: Continue differential and conformance-driven hardening.

entries.name: Type grammar parse-and-erase
entries.state: Type syntax is parsed for runtime erasure; no typechecker is intended for P1.
entries.future_plan: Defer gradual typechecker/LSP work to public-parity phase.

entries.name: Compiler
entries.state: The production compiler emits bytecode for the pinned corpus and discovers captured bindings before final lowering, enabling direct immutable captures while preserving mutable loop/backedge semantics.
entries.future_plan: Add differential/fuzz coverage for parser/compiler and runtime-error-phase parity, then harden diagnostics, O2 passes, superinstructions, and optimization boundaries.

entries.name: Bytecode dispatch core
entries.state: The portable big-match/br-table interpreter is authoritative. Bounded private HotIR numeric tracelets preserve logical fuel, deterministic-GC policy, and atomic fallback; a four-lane prototype-polymorphic call-site PIC plus direct immutable captures now accelerates the tracked closure workload.
entries.future_plan: Extend verified HotIR effect/control-flow coverage, add profile-led superinstructions/O2 and hot/cold split, and keep fuel, GC, coverage, and fallback semantics invariant.

entries.name: Value representation
entries.state: The sealed 16-byte tagged value, 13-byte inline binary strings, and shared compiled-string references are implemented, documented, and validated by an exact 512-VM Linux sampler.
entries.future_plan: Keep the representation sealed while expanding measurement to realistic mixed heaps and continuing GC work.

entries.name: Heap and GC
entries.state: Collection scheduling exists: Standard uses paced gc-arena debt collection, DeterministicSim uses instruction-count full cycles, and weak-table entries are swept. However, the VM's table/function/upvalue/coroutine slots, rooted atomized and non-inline runtime strings/userdata/buffers/vectors, and loaded-program store are append-only and are not reclaimed or reused until VM drop; aggregate heap accounting and quotas are absent.
entries.future_plan: Implement complete reachability and safe slot reuse, true public Function/Exports rooting or an ownership redesign, live/peak accounting, per-VM quotas, catchable or host-visible atomic OOM behavior, and native/wasm long-run plateau tests before tuning collection intervals.

entries.name: Tables/metatables
entries.state: Broad table, metatable, iteration, and stdlib behavior is conformance-covered. Logical deletion preserves tombstone insertion semantics, larger hash parts use a deterministic side index, and shape-revalidated positive string-slot caches cover global/index reads and writes plus dedicated GETTABLEKS, SETTABLEKS, and NAMECALL field/method paths. Exact OOP candidate ns/unit is 65.959% lower under its accepted Linux protocol; that comparison also includes the weak-table GC-scan correction.
entries.future_plan: Keep the full suite and exact protocol green, then add cached-length refinements and broader adaptive specialization.

entries.name: Functions/coroutines/pcall
entries.state: Functions, closures, varargs, coroutines, and protected calls have broad coverage.
entries.future_plan: Keep stackless recursion and yield paths covered as runtime changes.

entries.name: Base/math/string/bit32/vector/utf8 stdlib
entries.state: Major pinned Luau stdlib surfaces, including buffer, vector, utf8, and string pack/unpack behavior, are fixture-covered. Host-environment output/time services are now provider-backed: print composes tostring/__tostring into a host stdout sink (no-op without one), no-arg os.time/os.date read a wall-clock provider with a pinned-epoch fallback, and os.clock reads a monotonic provider with a deterministic logical-clock fallback. collectgarbage('count') remains zero and gcinfo memory reporting synthetic.
entries.future_plan: Keep the language-library corpus green while adding honest internal VM memory statistics with deterministic-profile policy.

entries.name: Error/debug behavior
entries.state: Debug/error behavior is substantially covered for conformance, and public rustia errors expose source-span/runtime-location accessors for diagnostic renderers.
entries.future_plan: Tighten VM stack traces and source diagnostics, and prove valid runtime failures remain catchable at runtime rather than moving into compile-time rejection.

entries.name: f64/libm/canonicalization discipline
entries.state: Deterministic number policy is documented and partly enforced by tests.
entries.future_plan: Keep compiler and VM on the same libm/canonicalization rules.

entries.name: Runtime profiles
entries.state: LuauCompat, ReproducibleStandard, and DeterministicSim are concrete runtime profiles. LuauCompat selects Luau-style hash iteration; DeterministicSim omits collectgarbage/gcinfo and optional loadstring, registers the os table iff a deterministic clock provider is plugged, admits a stdout sink on any profile, rejects nondeterministic clock providers, deterministically sweeps weak tables, and rejects external-mutable-state/nondeterministic-effect host registrations. Decision-reset behavior is not yet a complete replay ABI.
entries.future_plan: Specify exactly which globals, RNG, fuel, counters, programs, and heap objects reset at a deterministic decision boundary.

entries.name: Fuel and limits
entries.state: Instruction fuel exists and public host-function fuel metadata carries an ABI version. There is no aggregate heap/allocation quota or complete OOM contract yet.
entries.future_plan: Add versioned memory limits and atomic failure semantics alongside instruction fuel, then keep optimized instruction costs and decision resets replay-stable.

entries.name: Cross-engine wasm proof
entries.state: Production rustia wasm and call_ref vs br_table dispatch are measured across V8, JavaScriptCore-family, and SpiderMonkey; the pre-lock wasm gate is closed.
entries.future_plan: Keep the measurements fresh as the wasm artifact and runtimes evolve.

entries.name: Full target correctness and golden matrix
entries.state: Linux x86_64, macOS arm64, and wasm/V8 golden evidence exists, with retained JavaScriptCore-family and SpiderMonkey shell portability measurements. Hosted CI is Linux-only; Intel macOS, Windows, Linux arm64, mobile native, and real Firefox/Safari browser goldens are not all continuously covered.
entries.future_plan: Add reproducible cross-target builds and goldens for the full design/00-constraints.md matrix without mixing non-dedicated macOS/Windows timings into the benchmark history.

entries.name: Koto-shaped facade
entries.state: Builder, typed run<T>, source-named compile/run helpers, public error diagnostic accessors, globals, exports, retained functions, environment presets (standard/deterministic/live) with stdout and determinism-labeled clock service sockets, examples, and a first koto-to-rustia migration guide exist.
entries.future_plan: Add lifecycle/limit/module controls, stabilize names and error types, and expand migration guidance as the production gates land.

entries.name: Owned value firewall
entries.state: OwnedValue supports nil, booleans, numbers, UTF-8 strings, tree-shaped tables, scalar/Option/Vec/BTreeMap conversions, and typed table helpers. It does not faithfully represent binary strings, buffers, vectors, opaque userdata identity, non-scalar/identity keys, shared/cyclic table graphs, or live VM values.
entries.future_plan: Add bytes/buffers/vectors, opaque identity-safe userdata handles, richer keys, and graph-preserving shared/cyclic tables while keeping internal GC lifetimes behind the facade; full UserData/Scope registration remains optional later work.

entries.name: Typed host functions
entries.state: Plain Rust functions can be registered with typed args/results through arity 8, capability-specific facade helpers, fallible rustia::Result<T> returns, parameter-count metadata, Rust parameter/return type metadata, fallibility metadata, and conversion errors that name the host function plus argument or return position.
entries.future_plan: Keep tightening diagnostics and decide whether public signature metadata should grow beyond Rust type names.

entries.name: Extension/linker layer
entries.state: Namespaced extensions, coarse capabilities, pre-install function metadata including host-fuel ABI version, Rust parameter/return type names, fallibility, deterministic registration validation, and explicit external-state helpers exist.
entries.future_plan: Add migration docs and decide how much internal fuel schedule data should become public.

entries.name: Public host-bridge seam
entries.state: The generic seam for deterministic host functions, typed slots, capability names, and effect ordering is documented without public grabby types. Injectable output/time providers are now implemented (environment presets plus determinism-labeled ServiceClock sockets, with DeterministicSim rejecting nondeterministic providers), but the facade does not yet mechanically enforce scratch-heap reset or aggregate memory limits, and it still lacks honest internal VM memory telemetry and a cheap worker-local/per-call host context for mutable slot/effect state.
entries.future_plan: Add a decision-boundary reset contract, internal memory telemetry, per-call host context, and long-run lifecycle tests while keeping public rustia generic.

entries.name: Module loading and resolution
entries.state: CompiledModule install and hot reload exist, and the architecture correctly assigns resolution to host policy. There is no script-visible require resolver, execute-once cache, dependency/cycle handling, or versioned deterministic module policy.
entries.future_plan: Add a host-owned resolver/cache interface with deterministic identity, cycle diagnostics, capability policy, transactional installation failure behavior, and no implicit filesystem dependency in the core VM.

entries.name: Decision lifecycle and reset
entries.state: Hosts can drop and reconstruct a VM, and retained Function/Exports handles carry install-generation metadata, but there is no public reset/finish operation that discards transient programs, coroutines, globals, upvalues, and heap objects. Current facade generations alone do not make all raw retained handles safe for slot reuse.
entries.future_plan: Specify a versioned reset ABI and implement epoch-safe invalidation while preserving chosen settings, host extensions, and explicitly reusable immutable modules; prove flat memory across many decisions.

entries.name: Serde bridge
entries.state: Owned-value serde paths exist, and OwnedTable can deserialize string-keyed fields plus array slots through serde.
entries.future_plan: Add binary and graph-preserving owned serde, then a lifetime-safe live/zero-copy path after the public value surface stabilizes.

entries.name: Retained handles
entries.state: Script function and export handles can be retained, called, inspected for the install generation they came from, checked for freshness, accessed through fail-closed current-generation call/value/get/function/deserialize paths, and are covered by first-slice migration guidance.
entries.future_plan: Make retained handles true roots or redesign ownership before slot reuse; preserve ordinary cross-reload calls outside reset epochs and specify explicit reset invalidation.

entries.name: Hot reload
entries.state: Compile/install/hot-reload entry points and source-named run helpers exist; tests cover source-name diagnostics, public runtime-location accessors, failed-reload old-program survival, generation-stamped handles across successful reload, and stale-handle fail-closed calls/export access. Runtime-failing reload can still leave partial global/heap effects because execution is not transactional.
entries.future_plan: Add reclamation under repeated reload, true-root/epoch-safe retained handles, transactional or isolated runtime-failure semantics, module dependency behavior, migration docs, and broader install-time diagnostics.

entries.name: Macro/codegen sugar
entries.state: Macro sugar exists as an early slice, but the lower-level API should lead.
entries.future_plan: Delay expansion until the core API stops moving.

entries.name: Harness CLI and schema
entries.state: bench/ has a standalone-style CLI, package metadata, machine-readable inventory, validated JSONL history schema, refreshable RESULTS.md, current-results JSON, generated per-workload claim gating, retained fixed-work A/B evidence, and a separate paired many-VM memory evidence schema.
entries.future_plan: Keep JSONL as the source of truth for CI and website data.

entries.name: Adapter matrix
entries.state: All 12 requested adapters are implemented; mlua-lua54 runs as a separate binary from Luau because of mlua-sys linking constraints.
entries.future_plan: Split adapters into standalone crates/binaries and keep baselines current.

entries.name: Workloads
entries.state: Five default workload families are wired, with 18 workload entries present; the non-default #15 string-building/concat workload has source coverage and smoke-tested execution across all requested adapters, #16–#18 provide portable burst/churn/intentional-retention memory probes, and #19–#21 provide deterministic steady/history/intentional-retention todo-app probes for Luau and Koto.
entries.future_plan: Record the first coherent cross-engine Linux memory cohort, expand the remaining #12 interop, #13 serde, and #14 fuel/limit workload plan, then refresh intentional measurement history.

entries.name: History and static report
entries.state: A coherent Linux-only result snapshot at 83bc2f3 covers 12 adapter families plus a separately verified mlua/Luau JIT mode. Dirty-baseline guards, markdown and JSON results, interpreter-only and best-mode dashboard rankings, cold-start costs, claim gating, five default workloads, and exact matrix/dense/OOP/string/HotIR evidence are retained; the string-memory corpus remains evidence-only by design.
entries.future_plan: Publish long-run history and richer charts after standalone split.

entries.name: Benchmark operations
entries.state: Hosted CI validates committed benchmark artifacts without measuring. An explicit operator-started Linode lifecycle is the sole active measurement source and promotes only complete evidence after confirmed instance deletion. The isolated memory child/supervisor, cgroup-v2 sampler, repeated-epoch analyzer, publication schema, and dashboard are implemented; cohort pre-reclamation-18b58d8 published 110 rows from 990 fresh processes after independent local re-analysis.
entries.future_plan: Use the frozen memory baseline to gate bounded reclamation, keep the Linode lifecycle reproducible, accumulate longer coherent Linux history, and add regression alerts without mixing developer-machine timings.

entries.name: Wasm-emit JIT spike
entries.state: Runtime wasm emission is validated in spikes, not production-integrated.
entries.future_plan: Add type guards/deopt and interpreter-equivalence checks before production use.

entries.name: Native/wasm matrix
entries.state: A coherent 12-adapter-family native Linux baseline plus a verified mlua/Luau JIT mode is recorded; recurring wasm target results cover rustia+koto+rhai and br_table/call_ref dispatch on Node/V8, while the accepted four-runtime matrix remains archived as historical portability evidence.
entries.future_plan: Broaden public baselines and keep result history fresh across runtime updates.

entries.name: Workspace tests and release preflight
entries.state: Production crates have meaningful unit and conformance tests; just release-preflight composes release artifact checks, crate metadata checks, workflow policy checks, generated leaf package dry-run checks, explicit public-example compilation, and cargo test --workspace; hosted CI mirrors that gate.
entries.future_plan: Keep expanding tests with new runtime/API work and keep CI aligned with release-preflight.

entries.name: CLI
entries.state: rustia-cli supports file, stdin, --eval, and --repl execution with profile, fuel, source-name options, state-preserving line evaluation, expression shorthand, unit-tested parsing, and source-aware compile/runtime diagnostics.
entries.future_plan: Add richer multiline editing/history behavior and diagnostic formatting as VM stack traces mature.

entries.name: Live wasm demo
entries.state: demos/live-wasm can build and serve a browser demo outside normal workspace gates.
entries.future_plan: Refresh after production wasm/perf work and make it a public example.

entries.name: Crate publishability
entries.state: Workspace crates are still publish = false, but generated crate metadata audit, explicit internal dependency versions, publishability-derived leaf package dry-run checks in preflight/CI, package file-list audit, publishability blocker audit, release checklist, semver policy, changelog validation, and release preflight are present.
entries.future_plan: Flip policy only after P1 gates, then publish/remove internal dependency blockers in generated order.
